extracted.intended_audience: painters and visual artists (also poets, speakers, and students of art theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative principles for painters: how to study, what to represent, and how to make paintings communicate and move viewers. Includes related maxims about speech, patience, and the relative strengths of painting and poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study from nature, not other painters
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter's work will be of little merit if he takes the painting of others as his standard, but if he studies from nature he will produce good fruits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use painted pictures (masters' paintings) as your sole standard. Observe and copy nature directly. Example: Giotto studied animals and nature and thereby surpassed past masters; Masaccio demonstrated that setting any standard other than nature leads to decline. Anti-pattern: relying chiefly on imitation of other painters.

rubrics_metrics.name: All visible things belong to the science of painting
rubrics_metrics.description: Vastness of the field of painting: All that is visible is included in the science of painting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the scope of painting as encompassing every visible subject and phenomenon. This justifies broad study of forms, landscapes, light, and motion—anything perceivable by sight falls within the painter's domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting communicates directly through sight (no interpreters needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fruits of painting can be apprehended by all the populations of the universe because its results are subject to the power of sight... Therefore it needs no interpreters of diverse tongues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design compositions so that visual perception alone can convey meaning across cultures and languages. Use clear visual cues (gesture, light, composition) because sight is universally accessible; avoid over-reliance on textual explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting requires natural aptitude; cannot be fully taught
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting cannot be taught to him on whom nature has not conferred the gift of receiving such knowledge,... it cannot be copied, as letters can be, ... it alone remains noble, it alone confers honour on its author and remains precious and unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the role of innate visual talent: instruction and practice matter, but certain capacities (visual discrimination, imaginative perception) are prerequisites. Training should cultivate natural gifts rather than assume universal transmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to create convincing visual reality
rubrics_metrics.description: The imagination is to the effect as the shadow to the opaque body which causes the shadow ... painting produces them in a concrete reality outside the eye, so that the eye receives its images just as if they were the works of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for pictorial effects that make images appear real to the viewer—accurate form, convincing light, and credible detail. Use studies and observations that enable painted surfaces to 'act' like natural surfaces. Example: paintings that deceive animals and humans (dog greeting painted master) attest to this power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent works of nature with truth and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting represents to the brain the works of nature with greater truth and accuracy than speech or writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize fidelity to the observable properties of natural forms: proportion, texture, colour relationships, perspective, and how light affects surfaces. Accuracy in these elements increases persuasive and cognitive clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include surface, colour and shape as primary concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting includes in its range the surface, colour and shape of anything created by nature;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and build compositions with attention to surface treatment, accurate and harmonious colour, and correct shaping of forms. These are the 'primary truth' the painter seizes; weaknesses here undermine the work's credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painter must observe nature directly rather than rely on other sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: If thou wishest to go to nature, thou reachest her by the means of science, deduced by others from the effects of nature? And the painter, through himself alone, without the aid of aught appertaining to the various sciences, ... achieves directly the imitation of the things of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While other disciplines (geometry, anatomy, rhetoric, etc.) can assist, the painter's first and indispensable source is direct observation. Use scientific knowledge only as support, not as a substitute for looking at nature itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate movements to express mental attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the painting the movements are appropriate to the mental attributes of the figures which are engaged in any kind of action, there is no doubt that the deaf man will understand the action and intentions of the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose gestures, posture, and facial expression so they match the characters' inner states and intentions. Clarity of bodily expression is essential for conveying narrative and psychology without words. Anti-pattern: movements that contradict or fail to reflect the depicted emotion or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure clarity of action without words (visual narrative intelligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will appoint the man born deaf to be judge of painting, ... he will understand the action and intentions of the figures, but the blind man will never understand what the poet shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test compositions for self-contained legibility: could someone who only sees (and cannot hear labels or captions) understand the story? This is a criterion for successful pictorial storytelling—clarity, sequencing of action, and readable gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select medium by its strengths: painting for action/vision, poetry for words
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry surpasses painting in the representation of words, and in the representation of actions painting excels poetry; and painting is to poetry as actions are to words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the expressive medium according to the subject's core requirement: if the essential element is visual action, motion, or appearance, favor painting/visual representation; if the essential element is linguistic nuance or the play of words, favor poetry or prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paintings can evoke devotion and strong emotional responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When they are unveiled, the vast multitude of people ... prostrate themselves and worship and invoke those whom such pictures represent ... Therefore it appears that this deity takes pleasure in the pictures and is pleased that it should be loved and revered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use composition, scale, color, and iconography intentionally to elicit emotions and spiritual responses. Be aware of the painting's potential to move viewers beyond rational perception to ritual or devotional behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making imitation the goal; value originality and excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The arts which admit of exact reproduction are such that the disciple is on the same level as the creator... These are useful to the imitator, but are not of such high excellence as those which cannot be transmitted as an inheritance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not aim merely to reproduce the visible traits of a master or mechanical techniques. Seek originality in composition, handling, and interpretation; judge work by its unique quality and inventiveness rather than by fidelity to a single template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine observation with invention; painting can depict things nature never created
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting ... also infinite things which nature never created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While grounded in observation, painting has license to invent and imaginatively extend reality. Use imaginative invention to enhance meaning and visual effect, provided invented elements cohere with observed truth so they remain believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor speech and written argument to audience attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Words which do not satisfy the ear of the listener will always weary or annoy him; ... when you observe such signs of vexation, shorten your speech or vary your argument; and if you do otherwise, then instead of the favour you seek you will incur hate and hostility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting (or writing), monitor audience reactions. Shorten, vary, or change approach when attention flags (yawns, frowns). For writers: vary rhythm, sentence length, and subject matter to maintain reader engagement; avoid excessive length or monotony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience increases resilience under offense (virtue for creators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patience serves against insults as clothes do against the cold; ... let thy patience increase under great offences, and they will not be able to hurt your feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt patience as a working virtue: tolerate criticism and setbacks without letting them wound creative judgment. Cultivate increasing patience to withstand insults and obstacles in practice and reception of work.
